patch.title: Aratina 1: 200 MW Solar and 500 MWh Storage Online in July 2026
patch.description: Avantus announced commercial operations for Aratina 1 on July 20, 2026: 200 MW solar and 500 MWh storage. Its project website places the 350 MW two-phase program near Boron and Desert Lake in eastern Kern County, with Phase 1 operating and Phase 2 under construction.

references.title: Avantus’ Aratina 1 Project Officially Online, Generating Enough Clean, Reliable Energy to Power 105,000 California Homes
Aratina Solar Center — current project status
Aratina Solar Center — Proposed Sites maps
EIA August 2026 Inventory — Aratina 1A 68661 and 1B 61167
CAISO Public Queue — Aratina Solar Center 1 1204

patch.longFormSummary:
• EIA separately reports 120 MW solar / 75 MW battery at 1A and 80 MW solar / 50 MW battery at 1B, both operating July 2026; their battery energy totals 500 MWh. CAISO 1204 reports 200 MW solar and 125 MW storage, 200 MW export. Native power represents solar alone. EIA’s San Bernardino county/reporting point conflicts with operator Kern County maps; it is not used to relocate the site.
  • The prior 250 MW, $280M and October 2028 COD are unsupported. Financing commitments are not project capital cost. The pin dates the company’s operating announcement rather than asserting an exact earlier commissioning day.
  • Timeline: Confirmed July 20, 2026 announcement that Aratina 1 had achieved commercial operations; exact energization day is not independently established.
  • Operator proposed-site context diagram 1 for the overall Aratina program near Boron/Desert Lake. Not proof of built facilities or a verified phase-only surveyed boundary. Credit: Avantus / Aratina Solar Center; underlying aerial as shown.
  • Operator proposed-site context diagram 2 for the overall Aratina program near Boron/Desert Lake. Not proof of built facilities or a verified phase-only surveyed boundary. Credit: Avantus / Aratina Solar Center; underlying aerial as shown.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Confirmed July 20, 2026 announcement that Aratina 1 had achieved commercial operations; exact energization day is not independently established.
patch.address: Boron / Desert Lake, eastern Kern County, California; retained approximate project-area point, not a surveyed phase boundary

power.note: Operator 200 MW solar only; separate 125 MW / 500 MWh battery in EIA/CAISO, not additive export.

gaps: Resolve EIA San Bernardino county/reporting-point mismatch with operator Kern County site maps. Existing point is coarse context; no unsupported EIA relocation. Verify exact energization day and Phase 1 boundary.

patch.title: Aratina 2: 150 MW Solar / 452 MWh Storage, Late-2026 Target
patch.description: Avantus’s July 9, 2026 financing announcement confirms Aratina 2 under construction in eastern Kern County, with 150 MWac solar and 452 MWh battery storage, expected online by the end of 2026. EIA plant 64215 reports more than 50% construction complete and December 2026 operation target.

Aratina Solar Center — Proposed Sites maps

patch.longFormSummary:
• EIA identifies 45MG 8me LLC, 150 MW solar and 113 MW battery; CAISO 1604 lists Kramer 230 kV and December 31, 2026 proposed completion. Native power is solar only. More than $525M financing includes construction funding, bridge loan and letters of credit; it is not substituted for the unsupported $190M capital budget.
  • Timeline: Confirmed July 9, 2026 financing announcement, not exact COD. Operator end-2026, EIA December and CAISO December 31 are targets.
  • Operator proposed-site context diagram 3 for the overall Aratina program near Boron/Desert Lake. Not proof of built facilities or a verified phase-only surveyed boundary. Credit: Avantus / Aratina Solar Center; underlying aerial as shown.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Confirmed July 9, 2026 financing announcement, not exact COD. Operator end-2026, EIA December and CAISO December 31 are targets.

researchNotes: All 12 existing pins retained and corrected on local and production. Original authors preserved; live production title/source/author matched local snapshots. Reconciled all stale local IDs before mutation, re-read immediately before each write, and saved backups. No automatic merges, new pins or deletes.

Read August 2026 EIA generator inventory, September 2026 ERCOT GIS and CAISO primary workbook rows directly. Queue dates are projected CODs, not operating evidence. The same-day source files and row extracts are retained, including component MW versus combined export and EIA generator identifiers.

Aratina 1: Avantus announced July 20, 2026 commercial operations for 200 MW solar / 500 MWh storage, retaining a controlling stake. EIA divides it into 1A (120 MW solar, 75 MW / 300 MWh battery) and 1B (80 MW solar, 50 MW / 200 MWh battery), both July-2026 operating. Native 200 MW is solar alone; CAISO 1204 combined export is 200 MW. The saved date is the company announcement, not an independently verified energization day. EIA county/reporting point conflicts with the operator’s Kern County Boron maps; that mismatch is explicit.

Aratina 2: opened July 9, 2026 Avantus release confirms 150 MWac solar / 452 MWh storage, under construction and late-2026 target. EIA 64215 reports 150 MW solar / 113 MW battery, December 2026 and construction over 50%; CAISO 1604 targets December 31. More than $525M financing includes loans, bridge funding and letters of credit, not total project cost. The old reporting point is far west of operator Boron maps, so moved to explicitly approximate whole-program Boron context, pending phase-specific parcel evidence. Three operator proposed-site diagrams do not establish phase-only boundaries or completion.

ORD-01: downloaded and read the October 15, 2024 operator sheet at its working September-2025 upload path. It specifies 36 MW / 220,000 gross sqft and 18.5-acre shared campus; the April 19, 2022 launch release instead said 48 MW expandable to about 60 MW. Preserve the launch date and explicit rating conflict; do not assign campus 72 MW, 100+ MW potential or 170 MW substation service to this building. Removed modeled 50.4 MW and $1.36B.

DFW-01: opened 2015 operator release states November 23 grand opening with first-phase 12.5 MW and 108,000 sqft. These are saved as historical opening-phase metrics, not current maxima. The 2019 8 MW expansion is not silently summed to infer current 20.5 MW. Current operator confirms a shared 19-acre campus with DFW-02. The indexed 2024 sheet says 10 MW / 36 MW split but accessible retrieval failed with 404; it remains a specific research gap. Removed modeled 28.7 MW and $779M. Historical campus full-build figures are distinct.

PDX-01: January 10, 2023 operator announcement supports first-building planned critical capacity 72 MW, separate from a second 36 MW building on the 27-acre campus. July 23, 2024 is a topping-out report, not COD. Saved the confirmed primary announcement milestone and qualified planned capacity; removed modeled 100.8 MW, $2.73B and unsupported 480,000 sqft. Current operator lists BESS support without enough evidence for installed MWh or generator count.

Frederick IAD04: downloaded and read the 31.8 MB July 1, 2024 MDE air-permit application. It proposes 168 x 3 MW plus four x 1 MW emergency generators, with alternative manufacturer models; proposed backup capacity is not IT load. Current operator confirms 5601 Manor Woods Road and a 75-acre campus. No 82.8 MW or $2.73B basis; native power removed. Later references to IAD-06 / 72 MW were not automatically equated to this broader IAD04 scope. No installed generator count inferred. Census rural-address interpolation differed from campus context and was not adopted without parcel evidence.

Alamo City: May 19, 2026 company-syndicated release supports actual groundbreaking and a 120 MW / 480 MWh CPS contract. EIA and OCI portfolio retain 200 MW design scope; ERCOT 26INR0330 reports 128.2 MW and September 21, 2027, versus EIA July 2027. Preserve the scope/date differences and use directly announced contracted capacity. The $130M tax-equity investment is not a replacement capital-cost estimate. Ceremony photo does not show commissioned batteries.

Albatross: this 50.4 MW EIA unit corresponds to ERCOT 25INR0071, later targeting December 30, 2028, versus EIA December 2027. Operator currently lists a broader 208 MWac late-stage-development project targeting 2028; separate ERCOT BESS 2 is 159.6 MW. Those scopes are not silently merged or summed. Removed $75M, 200 MWh, four-hour and LFP claims; stock BESS image is not an adopted phase-specific photo.

Alina: current Advanced Power portfolio explicitly publishes 200 MW / 400 MWh battery, not 800 MWh, alongside 222 MWdc solar and 2028 target. EIA lists separate 200 MW solar and battery units with June 2028 and approvals not initiated. No summed export capacity, inferred construction or $250M cost. Operator’s Alina image is labeled Stock Solar Panel and was rejected.

Avant Prairie: EIA 68349 reports 200 MW / July 2029 / approvals not initiated. Later ERCOT 27INR0316 reports 201.72 MW / April 16, 2029, completed studies but no IA. OCI lists it under development. No $240M, 800 MWh or construction finding adopted. Native rating cites EIA separately from the later queue rating.

Adams Creek: current branch-specific operator website says construction began in 2026, 250 MW on about 1,800 acres, Oncor 345 kV and 2027 target, superseding EIA not-under-construction status. EIA 70300 gives June 2027 target. Removed 240 MW, 2,200 acres, 138 kV, $260M and November 2027. The unlabelled DJI-named aerial shows completed solar rows and is not verified as this project, so rejected alongside explicit Unsplash images. Generic process graphic was not adopted as site evidence.

Alira: EIA 63193 identifies Luminant Generation Company LLC, 222.8 MW, approvals pending, January 2030; no construction or October-2027 COD support. Removed $250M and the invented operator article. No current project-specific gallery located in Vistra/Luminant search.

Cleared 12 unsupported prices and four calculated energy rows per environment. Replaced all four datacenter metric rows to remove unsupported daily water, hardware and installed-generator assertions. Published historical/design scope is labeled; no metered consumption derived from capacity.

Four location changes required 12 replacement USGS maps: Census address/intersection context for ORD-01, DFW-01 and PDX-01, plus qualified whole-program Boron context for Aratina 2. Tiny rounding differences in other EIA points did not justify replacements. IAD04 and the remaining reported/county points retain 24 legacy maps. Exact boundaries remain research gaps.

Added 17 credited gallery assets after visual inspection and plain-curl byte comparison: six ORD-01 photographs, three DFW-01 equipment/fence/break-area photographs, three PDX-01 exterior photographs, one Alamo groundbreaking photograph, one DFW-01 exterior image labeled render by its operator and three Aratina proposed-site diagrams. No commissioning date, installed capacity, equipment count or measured usage inferred from images. Excluded ORD-02/03, DFW-02, Chicago image on Maryland page, generic global Avantus SEO hero and unrelated solar/battery imagery.

Access and research limits are recorded rather than treated as cancellation: old DFW/Hillsboro brochure paths return 404; Frederick county staff-report link could not be retrieved, but the MDE application was downloaded in full. Native power for IAD04 is removed until scope is resolved; none of these twelve supported identities needed a hold.
